seoTitle: robots.txt Encoding Checker: BOM and Hidden Characters
metaDescription: Find byte order marks, zero-width characters, curly quotes and non-ASCII paths that make crawlers ignore robots.txt lines. Free, in your browser.
intro: Scans a pasted robots.txt for characters you cannot see that break parsing, and can print a cleaned copy.
why:
A robots.txt that looks perfect can still fail. A byte order mark at the start, a zero-width space inside a path, a non-breaking space after the colon or a curly quote pasted from a document makes a line unreadable. Google treats a byte order mark as an invalid line.

The checker lists each odd character with line, column and code point, notes line endings and shows a cleaned version. Pasted text is already decoded, so a file saved in the wrong encoding shows up as replacement characters.
howTo: Paste the robots.txt, ideally copied straight from the live file.
Read the list of suspicious characters.
Use the cleaned copy as a starting point.
Save the file as UTF-8 without BOM.

faq.a: Google's documentation lists a byte order mark among invalid lines, so the first rule may be lost.

faq.q: Does it detect files saved as Latin-1?
faq.a: Only indirectly, through replacement characters after pasting. For a file on disk use the file command shown in the output.
No. Write them as percent-encoded UTF-8.
CR, LF and CRLF are all valid.
